commands.review_summary:
The branch removes the standalone Privacy status card, replaces the Location segmented picker with a single toggle and read-only Access Level row, adds a presentation helper and active-scene refresh behavior, and expands focused iOS tests.

PR surface: Other +459. Total +459 across 8 files.

Reproducibility: yes. Source inspection of the PR head shows the toggle only writes `.whileUsing` from off and the Access Level row is read-only, while current runtime code still requires `.always` for background location.
commands.review_followup: - The remaining blockers are concrete and localized: restore Always selection in the new card UI and sync native i18n without broadening the Privacy redesign.

target.title: feat: Privacy screen location controls
target.body: Fixes #103013. AI-assisted: Codex was used for implementation, testing, and simulator validation. ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where users opening iOS Settings -> Privacy saw a redundant standalone Privacy status card alongside separate Location controls containing overlapping information. The Location UI also mixed OpenClaw's sharing preference with the actual iOS authorization level, displayed unnecessary guidance after permission denial, and could make the Notifications section difficult to reach. ## Why This Change Was Made This makes the Location card the single source of truth for location sharing: - removes the redundant standalone Privacy status card - places the Location Sharing toggle directly on the Location row - presents Access Level as a read-only value - uses Apple's `While Using the App` and `Always` terminology - derives Access Level from the actual iOS authorization, including when OpenClaw sharing is off - hides Access Level and redundant guidance when permission is denied - opens the app-specific iOS Settings page when a user retries after denial - refreshes authorization state whenever the app returns to the active scene - keeps toggle-off as OpenClaw sharing intent without pretending to downgrade the OS permission - improves VoiceOver output, Dynamic Type wrapping, and loading-state layout stability - restores reliable scrolling to the top of the Privacy screen ## User Impact Users now see one clear Location section that distinguishes OpenClaw's sharing state from the permission retained by iOS. The screen accurately reflects permission changes made outside OpenClaw, avoids redundant denial messaging, remains accessible at larger text sizes, and keeps the Notifications section reachable. ## Evidence ### After: `openclaw-103013-refinements-final-large.png` Validation: - SwiftFormat lint passed for the touched iOS files - `git diff --check` passed - focused `xcodebuild` validation passed with 165 tests across `LocationPermissionSummaryTests`, `NodeAppModelInvokeTests`, and `SwiftUIRenderSmokeTests` - focused Privacy and Location source-contract coverage passed - built, installed, and visually verified on iPhone 17 and iPhone 17 Pro simulators running iOS 26.4 - simulator accessibility inspection confirmed a single VoiceOver Access Level element and value - Privacy rendering was checked across light and dark appearances and accessibility text sizes Known unrelated local baseline failures: - `RootTabsSourceGuardTests.local network access is requested from visible gateway flows` expects the existing `connect_last_known` source string - `OpenClawTypographyTests.iOS app text and control calls keep branded font boundaries` reports existing shared chat UI strings outside this PR's changed files
